items.diagram_kind: iterated point blowups and final strict-normal-crossing configuration
items.reason: The theorem constructs a finite sequence of point blowups and distinguishes the total transform from the strict transforms of the original curve components and the exceptional curves. Its terminal condition is local and incidence-based: each support point lies on one regular component or on two regular components meeting transversally. A staged diagram can clarify this geometry. The current render is prose-only. This is an editorial opportunity; the source states no uniqueness of the sequence, and no mathematical defect is alleged.

claim_lines.text: of blowups of $S$ at closed points such that:

is a regular curve, and at every closed point of the support either one component passes or
exactly two components pass and meet transversally.
Exceptional curves are regular and meet the strict transforms only
transversally, so no new singular one-dimensional components are created. The
conclusion is SNC support with regular irreducible components; the support
itself need not be regular at a crossing. No smoothness of the components over
a non-perfect ground field, relative SNC structure over a base field, or
resolution in dimension greater than two is asserted.

[F3] Point blowups of a regular surface stay regular surfaces, at centers of local dimension two their exceptional curves are regular curves (at local dimension one the blowup is the identity), and the blowup restricts to an isomorphism away from the center

[F4] Multiplicity drop and separation: if $Y$ is an integral curve and $\mathcal O_{Y,p}$ is regular at a closed point $p$ lying on a second closed subscheme $Z$ with $\eta_Y\notin Z$, then the strict transform $Y'$ meets the exceptional curve $E$ of the blowup at $p$ in exactly one point $q$ with $m_q(Y'\cap E)=1$, every point of $Y'\cap Z'$ over $p$ has multiplicity strictly smaller than $m_p(Y\cap Z)$, and if $m_p(Y\cap Z)=1$ then $Y'$ and $Z'$ are disjoint over $p$

[F5] Separation of components: for finitely many pairwise distinct integral one-dimensional closed subschemes with finite normalization there is a finite sequence of blowups at closed points whose strict transforms are pairwise disjoint regular curves

proof_step_locators.step: 2.1: separation of original curve components; selected blowup centers and regularity of total-transform support
3.1: total transform remains effective Cartier; support tracks strict transforms and exceptional curves centered on the preceding support
4.1: reduce maximum pairwise contact multiplicity by point blowups
5.1: remove triple points by blowing up their closed centers

staged_sequence: Show a finite but unspecified chain S_n → S_{n−1} → … → S_1 → S_0=S, with every arrow a blowup at a closed point p_{i−1} of the preceding regular surface S_{i−1}.

At each step distinguish the total transform Z_i (inverse image as an effective Cartier divisor), strict transforms of the original curve components, and the exceptional curve E_i over the center. E_i belongs to the total-transform support exactly when its center lies on the preceding total-transform support.

If depicting the proof stages, indicate component regularization/separation (step 2.1), contact-multiplicity reduction (step 4.1), and removal of triple points (step 5.1). These describe a valid existence construction; do not present the chosen sequence as canonical or unique.
End with local schematic panels for a point on one regular support component and a point where exactly two regular components meet transversally (m_p=1). Include that there are no triple points.
checks: Every displayed morphism has direction S_i → S_{i−1}; its center p_{i−1} lies on S_{i−1}, and the exceptional curve E_i lies on S_i.
Use total transform for the scheme-theoretic inverse image divisor and strict transform for the transformed original component; do not conflate them or erase multiplicities in Z_i.

The exceptional components of the support are those whose centers lie on the preceding total-transform support; a blowup away from the support is an isomorphism near the divisor and contributes no component to its support.
All S_i remain regular surfaces. Each irreducible support component is a regular curve, but the union/support can be singular at a crossing.

At each closed point of the final support there is either one component or exactly two; in the latter case they meet transversally, expressed in the proof as intersection multiplicity m_p=1. No point has three or more support components.
A local crossing sketch is schematic and does not assert component smoothness over the ground field, relative SNC over a base, or any resolution result in dimension greater than two.
The theorem asserts existence of a finite sequence, not a unique sequence or a canonical set of blowup centers.
